summary: S08-fleet-guard-reliability/spec.md amended (T803): added §2a (ORC-GD-1..5), a declared resource-need block set at registration as admission's primary control, upstream of the machine-danger floor. No code touched — this is a spec amendment only, per the brief's own scope limit; T786 owns the task fields, the S08 build passes own the code.

gap_measured.before: no field records what a task needs anywhere: caps=[] on all 434 tasks, expected_wall_s populated 0/417; the only live knobs are per-invocation flags with global defaults (--max-rss, --host-mem-floor-mb default hw.memsize // 8), never a per-task declaration.
gap_measured.design_defect: tools/runner:2731's host_total // 8 floor is a machine-level question (is the host in danger?) but tools/runner:3151's kill path (largest_pid = max(poll_rss, ...)) takes a task-level action with no comparison of that member's RSS against the shortfall anywhere in the path (tools/runner:3123-3196) — the two questions were never separated upstream of the existing ORC-G1..G10 response controls.

one_line_per_id.ORC-GD-1: declared-need block at registration: ram_mb required, cpu_s/max_siblings/wall_s optional
one_line_per_id.ORC-GD-2: defaults come from task type + provider, measured not invented — resident-model tasks from model-registry.md, API tasks from the per-provider rss_mb distribution computed below
one_line_per_id.ORC-GD-3: admission arithmetic as a formula: admit iff projected_available (host_avail - committed declarations - resident tenant charge - this task's declared need) >= the existing unchanged floor; no added spare constant
one_line_per_id.ORC-GD-4: the machine-danger backstop (ORC-G1/G2/G7/G8) is unchanged and is reached far less often once ORC-GD-3 runs upstream
one_line_per_id.ORC-GD-5: an overrun (actual RSS > declared) is logged as a declared_vs_actual defect record first, feeding the next round of defaults; a stop is a separate, [design-open] threshold (recommended 25%), not automatic

per_provider_rss_distribution.method: python3 over untracked/runs/*.json's rss_mb field (474/512 records carry it); provider resolved from the model field where present, else joined against docs/infra/managent/tasks.json's agent field by task-id prefix; 23/474 records left unresolved and excluded (not guessed) — stated, not silently dropped, per ORC-GP-4's own principle applied here
per_provider_rss_distribution.rounding_rule: recommended default = ceil(p90_nonzero_rss_mb / 256) * 256 — headroom to the next quarter-GB, no additional spare constant

table.caveat: n=9, low confidence, flag for re-measurement as ox-alpha volume grows

table.provider: qwen3.8:27b-mlx resident task's OWN dispatched pid (not the daemon)
table.recommended_default_mb: NOT USED — see resident_model_declaration below; declaring the task-pid figure here would be D1 again, just moved into a registration field

resident_model_declaration.non_monotone_evidence: ORC-G9 (S08 spec, pre-existing): same run climbs 36 -> 1890 -> 9206 -> 10153 MB then settles ~7825 MB — the live sample under-reports by roughly 2x even after stabilizing
resident_model_declaration.why_above_the_single_measured_instance: operator's own framing in the brief ('18 GB', '18-25 GB usage') sits above the one measured 15.6 GB instance; the amendment recommends the declared default track the operator's stated ceiling rather than the single sample, since the goal is a default that does not recreate D1 (a startup-race sample winning before the model is fully resident).

floor_decision.resolved: kept the floor's VALUE unchanged (total // 8, tools/runner:2731 — the 2026-07-29 kernel panic precedent stands); changed the floor's ROLE from sole/only admission signal to machine-danger backstop, with declared-need admission (ORC-GD-1..3) added as the primary, far-more-frequent control that runs upstream of it.
floor_decision.evidence_cited: the futile-kill census (S08 §1.2, pre-existing): 16/20 (80%) of identified kills were futile; the 2026-08-23 15:19:09 incident killed three lanes (639 MB combined RSS) that could not have cleared even one of their own shortfalls, while the true 15.6-18 GB qwen cause went untouched because nothing upstream of the guard ever asked what any task declared it would need.
floor_decision.counter_case_considered: a reasoned case for leaving the floor's role unchanged would need to explain that record; none was found — the amendment states this rather than assuming the change was needed.

what_this_would_have_changed_on_2026_08_: the qwen lane would have declared ram_mb ~= 18000 at registration (resident-model derivation) before any of the four lanes launched; ORC-GD-3's admission arithmetic, evaluated for the co-launch batch, would have shown projected_available falling below the floor once the qwen declaration and the three cloud lanes' own per-provider defaults were summed against the observed 5.4-6.0 GB available — using a number that does not depend on a ps sample winning a startup race. The batch would have been refused/queued at admission (T713's stance: stays dispatchable) and zero of the three 88-second kills at 251/133/129 MB RSS would have occurred, because none of those three lanes would have been running when the real 18 GB consumer was loading.
out_of_scope_respected: no edits to tools/runner, bin/subagent, or the task-store schema
no code changes of any kind — spec amendment only
the floor's numeric value (total // 8) is unchanged; a diff touching it still fails accept (S08 §10.5)
